mcqs.question: Two vectors A and B are drawn head‑to‑tail: vector A has magnitude 5 cm and points east, and vector B has magnitude 5 cm and points north. Using the graphical (head‑to‑tail) method, what is the direction of the resultant vector?
mcqs.explanation: When vectors are placed head‑to‑tail, the resultant is the vector drawn from the tail of the first to the head of the last. Here the resultant points exactly halfway between east and north, i.e., at 45° to the east (northeast). The other directions do not represent the correct geometric sum.

mcqs.question: A car moves from point A to B with a displacement of 8 km east (vector AB). It then moves from B to C with a displacement of 6 km north (vector BC). Which vector correctly represents the displacement from point C back to point A?
mcqs.explanation: The displacement from C to A is the negative of the resultant AB + BC. The resultant is 8 km east + 6 km north; its opposite is 8 km west and 6 km south. Options B, C, and D represent only parts of the required opposite vector.

mcqs.question: According to the triangle law of vector addition, the magnitude of the resultant vector is always equal to the sum of the magnitudes of the two individual vectors. Is this statement true or false?

options.C: It depends on the angle between the vectors
options.D: Only when the vectors are perpendicular

mcqs.explanation: The triangle law states that the resultant is obtained by placing the vectors head‑to‑tail; its magnitude equals the sum of the magnitudes only when the vectors are collinear and point in the same direction. In general, the resultant magnitude depends on the angle between the vectors, so the statement is false.

mcqs.question: Why does the parallelogram law give the same resultant as the triangle law for adding two vectors?

options.A: Because constructing a parallelogram places the two vectors tail‑to‑tail, and the diagonal represents the same head‑to‑tail addition as the triangle method.
options.B: Because the parallelogram law adds the magnitudes of the vectors directly.
options.C: Because the angle between the vectors becomes 90° in a parallelogram.
options.D: Because it only works for vectors of equal magnitude.

mcqs.answer: Because constructing a parallelogram places the two vectors tail‑to‑tail, and the diagonal represents the same head‑to‑tail addition as the triangle method.
mcqs.explanation: In the parallelogram method the vectors are drawn from a common origin; completing the parallelogram makes the diagonal from the common tail to the opposite corner identical to the vector obtained by the head‑to‑tail (triangle) construction. Options B, C, and D describe incorrect reasons.

mcqs.question: Which of the following situations is best solved using the polygon law rather than the triangle law?

options.A: Finding the resultant of three consecutive displacements applied one after another.
options.B: Adding two vectors that are already placed head‑to‑tail.
options.C: Determining the magnitude of a single vector.
options.D: Calculating the dot product of two vectors.

mcqs.answer: Finding the resultant of three consecutive displacements applied one after another.
mcqs.explanation: The polygon law extends the triangle law to any number of vectors placed head‑to‑tail, forming a closed polygon; the resultant is the vector from the start to the end point. Option B is essentially the triangle law, while C and D are unrelated to vector addition.

mcqs.question: Vector P has magnitude 30 N and points along the positive x‑axis. Vector Q has magnitude 40 N and makes an angle of 60° with the positive x‑axis. What are the magnitude (to one decimal place) and direction (to the nearest degree) of the resultant of P and Q?
mcqs.explanation: Components: P = (30, 0). Q = (40 cos60°, 40 sin60°) = (20, 34.64). Resultant components = (50, 34.64). Magnitude = √(50²+34.64²) ≈ 60.8 N. Direction = tan⁻¹(34.64/50) ≈ 34.8°, rounded to 35°. The other options do not match these calculations.

mcqs.question: What is the name of the graphical method used to add two vectors by placing the tail of the second vector at the head of the first?
mcqs.explanation: The head‑to‑tail (or tip‑to‑tail) method is the standard graphical technique for vector addition. The component method uses algebraic components, while scalar addition and dot product are unrelated to graphical addition.

mcqs.question: Subtracting vector B from vector A (A − B) is equivalent to adding which of the following to vector A?

options.A: The vector that has the same magnitude as B but opposite direction

mcqs.answer: The vector that has the same magnitude as B but opposite direction
mcqs.explanation: A − B = A + (‑B). Thus, subtracting B is the same as adding the vector that is equal in magnitude to B but points in the opposite direction. Options B, C, and D do not represent the correct operation.
